say: The Sun is too cold to shine. [0.5] ~And yet, it does.
Its core is fifteen million degrees. [0.3] That sounds hot.
But to fuse, two protons have to touch. And protons push each other away, hard.
Forcing them together should take about ten billion degrees. [0.45] ~The Sun is hundreds of times too cold.
So how does it burn? [0.5] The protons cheat.
It is called quantum tunnelling. A particle is also a wave, [0.3] and a little of that wave leaks straight through the wall.
It almost never works. A single proton can wait a billion years for its turn.
That is why the Sun burns so slowly. Litre for litre, your body makes more heat than its core.
But the Sun is enormous. [0.4] So every sunbeam you have ever felt [0.3] ~began with a particle walking through a wall.
